-# Set permissions to Managed Home Screen using Android Enterprise OEMConfig - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
+# Grant Android app permissions by using Android Enterprise OEMConfig - Microsoft Intune | Microsoft Learn
 
-The Managed Home Screen (MHS) is an Intune app that allows you to configure the home screen on the device. It only shows the apps that your users access and the device settings that admins need to manage.
+Use Android Enterprise OEMConfig in Microsoft Intune to grant app permissions on dedicated and fully managed devices without asking users to approve them manually. -The MHS is used for kiosk devices, including frontline worker (FLW) devices. It replaces the default launcher on your Android Enterprise dedicated and fully managed devices. +Before you begin, review the prerequisites later in this article. -Typically, when you configure the MHS on a device, end users need to manually accept certain permissions that MHS needs. These permissions allow the MHS to access device features and settings.
-
-Instead of relying on end users to accept the permissions, you can use an [OEMConfig device configuration policy](configure-oemconfig-android) to automatically grant permissions to the MHS app.
-
-This feature applies to:
-
-- Android Enterprise devices enrolled as [dedicated devices](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-dedicated)
-- Android Enterprise devices enrolled as [fully managed devices](../../device-enrollment/android/setup-fully-managed)
-

-

-- Zebra
-- Honeywell

messageCenterItems.title: Plan for Change: Update your iOS/iPadOS and macOS Company Portal minimum version to v5.2608.0
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting February 2027, the minimum iOS/iPadOS and macOS Company Portal version will be v5.2608.0. Most users update automatically; those with app installation blocked may need manual updates. Prepare by informing helpdesk and pushing updates if device restrictions are enabled.
messageCenterItems.body:
Updated November 16, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

To support the latest Apple OS releases, starting in early February 2027 (previously early December 2026), the minimum supported version of the iOS/iPadOS and macOS Company Portal will change to v5.2608.0. 

How this will affect your organization:

User impact: Most users have app updates set to automatic, so they receive the updated Company Portal app without taking any action. Users that have an earlier app version will be prompted to update to the latest Company Portal app. 

Note: If you have enabled the ‘Block installing apps using App Store’ device restriction setting, you may need to manually push an update to devices. 

What you need to do to prepare:

If you have enabled the above device restriction setting you will likely need to push an update to devices. Otherwise, no action is needed, but if you have a helpdesk, you may want to make them aware of the prompt to update the Company Portal app.
